agents.note:
US-530 CLOSED + COMMITTED as 5328330 (Sprint 71 / V0.29.26, 1/6 done). NO TD-059 STALL -- clean tree, built from scratch, kept the gate -> COMMIT -> bookkeeping ordering. NEXT: US-531 (token-gated write endpoint) -- it is the natural follow-on and I left it a ready-made seam.

WHAT SHIPPED: config.local.json, a FLAT dot-path overlay beside config.json (gitignored + excluded from BOTH deploy sync paths). effective = allow-listed overlay override ELSE config.json default, resolved by ONE function that both config readers call.

*** THE FLAT-KEY CHOICE IS THE HANDOFF TO US-531. *** A nested overlay mirroring config.json would need a recursive walk to answer 'is this key overridable?', and the write endpoint would inevitably grow a SECOND walk that drifts from the read one. Flat dot-paths make the allow-list a literal key comparison, so US-531 imports validateOverlayValue(key, value) -> (ok, stored) and overlayPathFor(configPath) and writes ZERO new validation. IF THE NEXT ITERATION RE-IMPLEMENTS THE ALLOW-LIST IN states_http_server, THE DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH CLAIM BECOMES TWO GATES THAT CAN DISAGREE -- which is worse than one, because it looks stronger. US-531 still owes: token gate (_tokenOk, US-403/407 pattern -- NEVER weaken it), atomic temp+rename write, and returning the REAL stored effective value (re-resolve after writing; do not echo the request).

MUTATION A IS THE LESSON AND IT IS A NEW SHAPE OF THE RECURRING ONE. Two INDEPENDENT READERS of the same fact cover for each other in a per-reader test suite. I dropped applyConfigOverlay from _loadDisplaySection: 3 red, but test_loadConfigWithSecrets_appliesOverlay STAYED GREEN -- a suite with one test per reader ships the exact A-4 divergence the story exists to prevent. The test that actually pins it is a PARITY test asserting both readers return the IDENTICAL value. It is parametrized [0, 8, 20] on purpose: 8 IS the shipped default, so a parity test using only 8 passes with a completely broken reader. GENERAL RULE, NEW: when N consumers must agree on one fact, assert the AGREEMENT, and choose a fixture value that DIFFERS from the default -- a test whose expected value equals the fallback proves nothing.

MUTATION C RESTATES THE DECLARATION-VS-MECHANISM RULE IN ITS PUREST FORM. I removed the invalid-power-mode coercion to 'unknown'. 6 red -- and the WARNING log STILL SAID 'resolving to unknown' while the code no longer did. The log is a declaration; only the assertion pins the mechanism. Do not let a log line stand in for a test. (Mutation B: drop the seam from loadConfigWithSecrets -> 4 red. All three reverted BY HAND -- git checkout is outside the allow-list -- and re-verified green + `git diff` clean.)

THE TAR FALLBACK HAD A SECOND HOLE I ALMOST MISSED. deploy-pi.sh has TWO sync paths (rsync, and tar-over-ssh when rsync is absent locally). Excluding config.local.json from the TARBALL is NOT enough: the fallback WIPES the remote top level before extracting, so the overlay also needed a `! -name 'config.local.json'` in the preserve `find`. Without it, any deploy from a machine without rsync silently deletes the operator's settings -- a data-loss bug that no tarball-exclude test would catch. CARRY THIS: when a script has a primary and a fallback path, a durability guarantee must be re-proven in BOTH, and 'excluded from the copy' is not the same guarantee as 'survives the delete'.

REAL-CONFIG SMOKE BEYOND THE FIXTURES (worth repeating for config work): planted an overlay next to the SHIPPED config.json. Both readers returned autoRotateS=0 + power.mode=wall; the planted out-of-allow-list pi.obd.port was rejected + logged ONCE PER READER (proving both gates fire) and raised KeyError('obd') = the rejection invented no config branch. `git status --ignored` showed `!!` -- git ACTUALLY ignores the file, which is the mechanism behind my .gitignore-line assertion. Artifacts deleted.

GATE, SYNCHRONOUS, IN-LOOP, BEFORE THE COMMIT: RED first for the right reason (ModuleNotFoundError, not a typo). Then story file 42 passed / ZERO skips; consumer suites of BOTH touched readers (tests/test_secrets_loader.py + tests/pi/splash + test_config_validator + test_display_autodim_config) = 360 passed, 1 skipped. That 1 skip is PRE-EXISTING (test_token.py:70 POSIX file-mode on Windows, same one US-525/528 documented). ruff clean on all 4 .py files. `bash -n deploy/deploy-pi.sh` clean -- pytest CANNOT see a shell syntax error, so any .sh edit needs this. validate_config.py passes through the new seam.

BLAST RADIUS FLAGGED FOR PM: loadConfigWithSecrets is the project-wide config entry point = a BASE-MODULE change. PM should prioritize the full suite at integration. Behaviour is a strict no-op with no overlay file present (the shipped state), which bounds the risk.

LIVE VALIDATION OWED: the AC's 'overlay survives an rsync' is asserted against deploy-pi.sh TEXT, not a real rsync -- the real proof is the PM's Pi deploy (set autoRotateS=0 in config.local.json on the Pi, deploy, confirm it survives and both readers read 0). Remember a carousel-config change ALSO needs an eclipse-states-http bounce (config injected + cached at that unit's startup) -- that is US-533 GAP 1 and US-536's deploy note, and it will bite the first person who tests auto-rotate without bouncing.

ENVIRONMENT: `make` is NOT on PATH -- `make lint` exits 127, which READS LIKE A PASS. Use `python -m ruff check` directly. TD-075 still open: `ruff check src/ tests/` exits 1 on a CLEAN tree (10 pre-existing errors), so lint is per-touched-file. On this SMB share use per-suite runs + `-p no:cacheprovider` + an EXPLICIT timeout, or a long run gets auto-backgrounded and the result is lost (TD-059). Heredocs, not PowerShell here-strings, for multi-line git messages from the Bash tool.

FOR PM: a new inbox item appeared mid-iteration whose filename names US-536's subject (Atlas RCA -- --disable-gpu crashing the renderer). Not my lane to read; flagging only because US-536 is disposition-B REVERTING --disable-gpu, so it may bear on that story. Read before dispatching US-536.
